name: 11-pushed-number-then-server-create
why: THE SEAM NO SYNC-ONLY VECTOR REACHES, and Tracker shipped it wrong. A pushed issue carries the number it had in .issue.db. The server's counter never issued that number and does not know about it, so allocating the next number from the counter alone REISSUES one that already exists -- and the insert dies on the project's (project_id, number) unique constraint. Tracker's real server returned 500 internal_error on the first request that hit it, against a database holding rows the counter had not issued. NO FIXTURE COULD HAVE CAUGHT IT: every test created issues through the counter, which keeps it in step by construction, so the suite was structurally incapable of producing the state. It is a CONTRACT fact, not an implementation detail: a client may push any local number and must be able to rely on the server never reusing it. The server's counter is an OPTIMISATION FOR FINDING THE NEXT NUMBER, NOT THE AUTHORITY ON WHICH NUMBERS EXIST. Vectors 1-10 cover uid derivation, tombstones, direction and cursors; none of them reaches this seam, because it only appears where a pushed issue meets a locally created one. The push response now REPORTS the number the server settled on, which vector 12 makes load-bearing: a client that assumed its local number was always accepted would have no way to learn otherwise.
requires_note: The steps marked `requires: session` are SERVER-SIDE CREATES -- what the web UI does. They need a BROWSER SESSION, not a trk_ API key: /v1/projects/{org}/{project}/issues authorizes a user, and a sync key carries no user. That is deliberate and must not be relaxed to make this vector runnable -- a sync key already creates issues through push, and widening a credential for a test's convenience is the thing this contract refuses everywhere else. A client holding only an API key MUST report these steps as SKIPPED with the reason, never substitute a credential, and never score them as passed. Tracker covers the same seam in its own suite, where a session is available.
